comparison: Both address the circuit construction methodology (C59, C60, C63, C64, C65, C67). OpenEval finds the approach methodologically sound and SUPPORTED despite noting lack of biological justification for some parameters. Peer reviewers find it UNSUPPORTED, fundamentally challenging the addition of virtual nodes and questioning whether results depend on this methodological choice without clear justification.

Both evaluate the signal mobility edge and WDTM findings (C3, C24, C25, C27). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by computational data in Figure 2, treating them as valid novel contributions. Peer reviewers rate them UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the mobility edges are artifacts of the tight-binding approximation and stating 'the strength of the evidence presented in favor of interference effects being a major component in subthreshold wave dynamics is inadequate.'

Both address the comparison between effective conductance and interference-based transmission (C50, C51, C52, C53). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as a key contribution showing complex connectivity reduces wave transmission. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, fundamentally questioning why the quantum formalism was used instead of resistor-based representation and noting the authors 'have not tested' the alternative approach.

Both evaluate speculative claims about inferior olive and C. elegans oscillations (C54, C55, C56, with C16 overlap). OpenEval rates these UNCERTAIN, acknowledging they are explicitly speculative and lack data support. Peer reviewers rate them UNSUPPORTED, explicitly challenging these connections and questioning why C. elegans connectome was used for inferior olive-motivated questions, emphasizing 'No subthreshold oscillations were identified in the C-elegans.'

Both address WDTM patterns showing regular distance multiples in body-wall muscles (C4, C29, C30). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by Figure 3 data as key findings. Peer reviewers rate them UNCERTAIN, not directly validating the anatomical findings but questioning the model's biological relevance and noting 'the preprint falls short of relating its numerical results to any phenomena which could be observed in the lab.'

OpenEval addresses hmc connectivity and hub role (C32, C33, C36, C37, C45, C46) finding them SUPPORTED by network analysis. Peer R3 partially overlaps (C32, C33, C36, C37) but rates UNCERTAIN, expressing concerns about biological relevance rather than validating specific anatomical findings.

OpenEval addresses hmc as major hub (C45, C46) finding it SUPPORTED. Peer R4 includes these claims among hub findings rated UNCERTAIN, questioning the overall framework's validity and biological meaning of computational hub identification.

Both address long-distance transmission neurons (C35, C38, C39). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by Appendix 1-table 5 data as concrete findings. Peer reviewers rate them UNCERTAIN as part of broader concerns about the framework's biological validity and lack of connection to observable phenomena.

OpenEval addresses hub appearance rates and interference mechanisms (C40, C41, C42, C43, C44, C5) finding them SUPPORTED. Peer R3 partially overlaps (C41, C42, C44) rating UNCERTAIN, questioning biological relevance and parameter motivation rather than validating specific findings.

OpenEval addresses hub identification and mechanisms (C40, C41, C5) finding them SUPPORTED. Peer R4 overlaps on these claims rating them UNCERTAIN, questioning the framework's biological impact and noting lack of wavenumber estimation for C. elegans.

Both address the interference mechanism principle (C43). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED as physically sound. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, not disputing the physics principle itself but questioning whether the tight-binding approximation is justified in this biological context.

OpenEval addresses specific hub cell-pairs and the insight that strong edges don't guarantee hub status (C47, C49) finding them SUPPORTED. Peer R4 includes these among hub findings rated UNCERTAIN, questioning biological meaning of computational results without validation.

OpenEval finds background claims about C. elegans connectome, electrical synapses, and Anderson localization (C1, C2, C6-C20) SUPPORTED by appropriate literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these foundational claims.

OpenEval addresses computational error reporting (C70) finding it SUPPORTED as transparent disclosure with conservative correction, though noting unexplained root causes. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
